key_insight: MLLM failures on fine-grained questions often come from an inability to focus on small, decisive regions in full images rather than from lacking local recognition; Vision-OPD closes this regional-to-global perception gap by using on-policy self-distillation so the full-image model learns from its own evidence-centered crop-conditioned answers.
problem_solved: Improves multimodal LLMs' fine-grained visual understanding by enabling them to locate and use small but crucial visual evidence in full images without requiring extra human crop annotations.
method: Detect evidence regions implicitly (e.g., attention/saliency or model-suggested crops) and generate evidence-centered image crops.
Obtain more accurate crop-conditioned answers and use them as pseudo-teacher targets.
On-policy self-distillation: train the full-image model to match crop-conditioned predictions, iteratively closing the regional-to-global perception gap.
impact: Enables more reliable, explainable MLLM performance on tasks that hinge on small visual cues (e.g., detail-oriented VQA, fine-grained captioning) while reducing reliance on manual supervision—practical for deployment and continued model refinement.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: full image -> evidence detection -> crop -> crop-conditioned answer -> distillation back to full-image model
Before/after example pairs: same question answered incorrectly on full image but correctly on crop, then corrected after Vision-OPD training
Attention/heatmap overlays showing shift of focus from noisy regions to decisive evidence
Bar chart or table comparing accuracy on fine-grained benchmarks pre- and post-distillation (relative improvement)
paper_title: Vision-OPD: Learning to See Fine Details for Multimodal LLMs via On-Policy Self-Distillation
paper_authors: Qianhao Yuan, Jie Lou, Xing Yu, Hongyu Lin, Le Sun
